title: Script to change the tile size or alter sprite size?

posts.author: AmeerAshourDraws
posts.body:
I've recently gotten RPG Maker VX Ace with the Luna Engine as I've been thinking about messing around with them after seeing them on a huge sale on Steam. Looking forward to giving it a try as I'm also thinking of learning Ruby along with JavaScript!
Anyway, I have been wondering if there is a script to change the tile size or at least change the sprite size via code as I've been planning to make the game completely hand drawn with my own art (like actual hand drawn art not pixel art). I saw a plugin for MZ that alters the grid size to your liking and I was wondering if VX Ace has something similar. This specifically for reference:
Change Tile Size
Tile Size Version 1.0 by Fomar0153  Description Allows you to use tilesets of different sizes in RPG Maker MZ.  Features Easily use resources from older rpg makers!  Screenshots   Top: 64px tile; Bottom: 32px tiles  How to Use Place the plugin in your project's js/plugins/ folder. Inside RPG...
forums.rpgmakerweb.com
If there isn't, then at least a script that can change the sprite's scale with some code, and yes, I've also seen the same for MZ with one of MogHunter's MZ plugins.
If anyone knows anything resembling those for VX Ace, that will be appreciated!

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Can you explain the second part? What would the script accomplish
vis-a-vis
the sprite? I assume you mean the characters' sprites - those can already be any size, so long as you follow the spritesheet format outlined in the instruction manual.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
the VXA display library is closed source, so nothing can change it.
to change the tile size, you'll need access to the graphics library and that is not possible by default. However there was a project to replace the original VXA library with an DirectX-compatible one. That one is open source, but I don't know if it has an option to change tilesize - and even if it does nothing can change the editor, so you'll have to work with two tilesets of different sizes exchanged at runtime.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
I'm with Turan on this. I am failing to understand what you are trying to accomplish with the scaling sprites.
For the record, there are a fixed number of pixels; The only difference between "hand drawn" art  (which I will refer to as rasterized art) and "pixel" art is the resolution; or the number of pixels.
When you shrink art down to [roughly] the number of pixels of most pixel art...is it not just "pixel art" at that point?
Now, to be fair, I have not used VX Ace much at all, but from what I understand is that it has a maximum possible resolution that is still probably too small for rasterized art - and on most modern displays the max resolution is barely larger than a postage stamp.
It is not built with the intent of using rasterized art, so I am not sure why you are so excited to go back to an earlier Maker when (according to your profile) you have a Maker version that is more suitable for rasterized art.
Regardless, you would need to go into a photo editor and shrink your art yourself, but of course to be able to fit it into the resolution of the game is likely going to lose a lot of quality when you shrink it.
